title: Navigraph: Console IA for workspace switching, rollouts, and billing lenses
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Summary: Propose a consolidated information architecture ("Navigraph") that reduces navigation friction across workspaces, surfaces cost and billing lenses, and makes rollout controls discoverable and consistent. Currently: the left rail is dense, the rollout controls are buried inside project settings, and cost views are scattered across routes. This causes longer task times for SREs and platform engineers when diagnosing cost regressions or executing controlled rollouts.

Goals: (1) Provide a single, predictable place for operational workflows (dashboards, rollouts, incidents). (2) Make cost signals first-class via a Cost Hub with per-route token breakdowns. (3) Maintain fast workspace switching for cross-tenant teams while preserving scoped rollouts. (4) Create a design that is implementable without large platform schema changes.

Proposed IA: The "Navigraph" is a hybrid-left-rail with two semantic tiers: Global Hubs and Workspace Lenses. Global Hubs (top-level icons) house system-wide views (Overview, Cost, Incidents, Account), while Workspace Lenses are workspace-scoped routes (Models, Endpoints, Rollouts, Telemetry). Selecting a Global Hub preserves a small persistent breadcrumb that allows quick workspace context switching. Route pattern examples: /app/:workspace/hub/:hubId and /app/hub/:hubId (global).

Key UI patterns: (A) Persistent mini-switcher — a compact workspace chip with fast keyboard nav. (B) Cost Hub — primary landing that aggregates token spend by route, model, and time window with top KPIs and quick links to cost-optimizations and Optimize suggestions. (C) Rollouts lane — surfaced under Workspace Lenses with canary/toggle controls, audit snapshot, and golden-metric previews. (D) Compact rail collapse — preserves icon-only state but keeps the mini-switcher and search. (E) Command palette integration for jump-to-route and rollouts actions.

Design trade-offs: We intentionally move some global controls up one level to reduce deep navigation, which increases top-level complexity. Trade-off analysis: more discoverable rollouts vs slightly larger left rail. We reduce clutter by collapsing rarely-used admin routes into an "Administration" hub rather than mixing them with developer pathways.

Accessibility: All new controls follow 4.5:1 contrast, focus-visible for keyboard users, and aria-live notifications for rollout state changes.

Implementation notes: Minimal backend changes required — most routing is UI-only, but rollout audit snapshots will need a lightweight read endpoint (ENG-78902). Cost Hub requires per-route aggregation endpoints (ENG-78021). We recommend a staged rollout for this IA: A/B test between current nav and Navigraph for a subset of internal teams, collect task completion time and support tickets.

Metrics to measure success: time-to-switch-workspace, time-to-find-rollout, rate of accidental rollout toggles, Cost Hub adoption (DAU/MAU), and reduction in cost-related support tickets. Success thresholds: 20% reduction in time-to-find-rollout and 35% increase in Cost Hub DAU in 6 weeks.

Deliverables for review: high-fidelity Figma prototype, annotated IA map, click-through task scripts for usability test, and a small engineering spike for rollout snapshot API.

Open questions: Should the Cost Hub expose live token pricing? (privacy/cost concerns) — early recommendation: summarize spend with links to detailed billing exports. Should rollouts be globally searchable across workspaces? (we propose workspace-scoped by default with an opt-in global index for platform admins).
